# Microsoft FileServer protocol campaign

Independent audit correction (same campaign): the historical 297-case results below are preserved. Current source-call links and corrections are described in [the inventory audit](upstream-inventory-audit.md); an existing registration name proves neither identical input nor identical expected result.

Pinned first-party source: [WindowsProtocolTestSuites FileServer](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsProtocolTestSuites/tree/29ddb4238a5443b7499e82934c90cc898861c5e7/TestSuites/FileServer), revision `29ddb4238a5443b7499e82934c90cc898861c5e7`.
The complete recursive Git tree was fetched, not inferred from README text. All **406 C# source files** below `TestSuites/FileServer/src` were downloaded into the new campaign evidence directory and verified against their Git blob IDs (406 matches, zero mismatches), as well as SHA-256. Twelve relevant PTF configuration files were also downloaded and blob/SHA-verified; the FSA deployment InvalidName fragment and adapter enum numeric values were checked explicitly. The old campaign evidence was read only.

The inventory includes handwritten `SMB2`, **all `SMB2Model` generated families**, `Auth`, FSA `FileInformation`, `QueryDirectory`, `CreateFile`, `AlternateDataStream`, `CommonAlgorithm`, `FileAccess` (including IPC pipe opens), and the corresponding FSA model create/close/read/write/flush/query/set/rename/delete families. Other FileServer protocols (DFS referrals, shared VHD, VSS, storage QoS, cluster failover) and unrelated FSA control/volume/quota models are outside this allocation. There is no claim to have run Microsoft's MSTest/PTF runner or to have passed FileServer, FSA, or an entire generated state graph.

The scope includes authentication: NTLM/SPNEGO, key/session lifetime, integrity/signing, encryption and negotiation. Kerberos/domain ticket infrastructure and Windows ACL/claims SUT control are concrete blockers, not a blanket security exclusion. Ordinary tests use only offline .NET 10/BCL and existing fixtures. No upstream implementation, adapter DLL, downloader or external evidence path is a maintained test dependency. All assertions added here concern SMB packets, statuses, content, metadata, notifications or connection behavior; host bytes corroborate protocol effects. `P2Tests.Direct` establishes an authenticated session before dispatch and does not itself prove external authentication interoperability. Real TCP cases retain required signing and anonymous/Guest rejection. The TCP peer reuses `NtlmClient` only to construct credential proofs; SMB headers, SP800-108 derivation, transcript hashing, HMAC/CMAC/GMAC, AEAD transforms and compression encoding/decoding are independent test code.

## What counts as an adaptation

One maintained case can cover several equivalent upstream selectors; a generated model may repeat the same adapter operation through many graph prefixes/configuration branches. The tables retain **3,205 registered entry methods in 176 files**. Their current input links use **2,224 distinct normalized adapter/client member-call signatures**, including reachable private continuations/checkers, extracted while treating strings/comments as tokens. This includes configuration/assertion calls and is not a count of protocol scenarios. The historical regex extraction reported 2,694 entries and included at least 144 non-call/prose/property fragments; it is superseded by the [independent audit](upstream-inventory-audit.md). They do not count those source graph positions as independent passing tests. The disposition is for the public protocol partitions identified by its exact local cases. The original graph's `ReadConfig`, TestManager checkpoints, private model state and client bookkeeping are not adapted as server tests. Unsupported configuration arms (CA/persistence, resilient handles, application-instance fencing, forced-Level-II/SOFS, directory leasing, NTFS/ReFS-only controls, signing-disabled/Guest-success policy) remain explicit even when another arm uses an ordinary protocol operation.

An `already covered` reference names actual registered cases, audited against `--list`, rather than a suite or class name. It identifies the relevant public input/output invariant; it is not a claim that the source TestManager graph was executed byte-for-byte. New rows preserve independent source/spec expectations. A failing prerequisite is reported where it happens, not retried away or converted into an expected pass.

## Maintained groups and applicability

| Group | Public contract |
|---|---|
| Directory | Five additional ordinary FSCC layouts times seven wildcard partitions; all six supported layouts have bounded single-entry metadata pages, complete-record retry and cursor exhaustion. Existing FileNames wildcard cases are referenced, not repeated. Dot entries, exact names, EOF, file attributes and stable IDs are checked independently. |
| Data/metadata | Truncate/extend through peer opens, zero-filled holes, zero-byte writes, explicit EOF append, flush/stale FileId, offset/range validation, explicit timestamps, zero sentinels, creation/modification time, stream sizes/base-attribute identity, EA update/replace/delete and invalid name/flags, FileAllInformation granted access, fixed SET minima, normalized-name rejection, and CLOSE attribute/zero-field flags. Allocation remains an explicit unsupported backend capability, already checked by P5. |
| Native notify | Six signed TCP operations mutate actual LocalFileStore objects and await actual OS watcher responses: file/directory name, attributes, size, last-write, last-access. No sleeps or fabricated watcher events establish these cases. Creation/birth-time, EA/security/stream notifications retain their host/platform restrictions. Existing cancel/close/teardown cases are mapped exactly. |
| Context/state | Unknown and malformed CREATE contexts, actual durable grants followed by mixed reconnect contexts and valid retry, replay changes to name/attrs/disposition/oplock/CreateGuid in SMB300/302. File identity/recovery state is obtained through CREATE, not inserted into private managers. |
| Auth/negotiation | Five dialects; independent successful response signatures, bad signatures, SMB311 signing algorithms/ciphers, context cardinality/length/overlap, greatest-common offers, initial/unknown/retired sessions, reauthentication, PreviousSessionId, binding state/dialect/identity/channel keys, encryption-policy/dialect/capability partitions, encrypted file operations and compounds, all eight ValidateNegotiateInfo scenarios, all four client SecurityMode bit combinations in both negotiation and setup with required server signing retained, signed initial NEGOTIATE/SESSION_SETUP rejection, and incapable-client encrypted-share denial. Cross-source NTLM proof/invalid-token/SPNEGO cases are referenced from the Go/Samba owners. |
| Compression | Negotiated LZNT1/LZ77 literal-only request encoding, independent response decoding, small/large/incompressible/prefix partitions, REQUEST_COMPRESSED response choice, encryption-over-compression nesting and malformed transforms; invalid/unsupported negotiation inputs. Huffman response encoding and chained/PatternV1 negotiation are unavailable; they are not reported as passing. |

## Independent requirements and source differences

The captured [MS-SMB2 2025-07-07 specification](https://winprotocoldoc.z19.web.core.windows.net/MS-SMB2/%5BMS-SMB2%5D-250707.pdf) supplies mandatory context cardinality, no-common-dialect status, repeated-NEGOTIATE disconnect, binding state/identity/key rules, normalized-name unsupported status, CLOSE fields and ValidateNegotiateInfo disconnect rules. Its section 3.3.4.1.1 requires zero SMB header signatures inside encrypted messages. AEAD integrity does not waive that field rule.

[MS-FSA EOF processing](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fsa/5555bcb6-bc29-4f8a-900c-e469b792faab) and [FileBasicInformation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fsa/a36513b4-73c8-4888-ad29-8f3a196567e8) determine fixed SET sizes and invalid values; [FileAllInformation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-fscc/95f3056a-ebc1-4f5d-b938-3f68a44677a6) embeds actual per-open access. [MS-XCA 2.4.4](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/openspecs/windows_protocols/ms-xca/34cb9ab9-5ce6-42d7-a518-107c1c7c65e7) independently requires shared-nibble LZ77 extended lengths; the maintained decoder follows that format rather than the production codec.

The FileAllInformation empty filename expectation is a SHOULD with Windows-specific upstream branches; it is not asserted as mandatory. Reauthentication of a valid session is a SHOULD in MS-SMB2 3.3.5.5: its positive source-compatibility case remains visible, but rejection alone is not mislabeled a MUST violation. Invalid credit sequence disconnect and invalid impersonation-level rejection also have SHOULD/platform distinctions. The negative ByteOffset append-sentinel case follows the Windows object-store mapping in MS-SMB2/MS-FSA and is a compatibility finding, not a portable mandatory append-position claim. An append-only handle with an explicit offset is not assumed to force the Win32 implicit-append position.

Upstream `-2` timestamp helpers explicitly gate success to NTFS/ReFS. Three exploratory `resume-time` failures were rejected as inapplicable portable oracles and removed from registration, with original logs retained. Values below `-2`, zero no-op and portable `-1` last-write suppression remain distinct. Independent ChangeTime setting is explicitly unsupported. Birth-time setting and Windows automatic-access update scheduling are not inferred from LastWriteTime. Named streams/EAs are process-memory metadata; no process-restart persistence claim is added.

These historical counts are not the final registered total. Initial large I/O lacked advertised LARGE_MTU; the corrected client explicitly offers it and advances MessageIds by CreditCharge. Empty/truncated initial NTLM tokens were not assigned a fabricated universal LOGON_FAILURE status; duplicate cases were removed in favor of the independent Go/Samba cases.

The live Go/auth recheck used a newer source baseline and passed 26/29. Its build and run production hashes were stable. Relative to the frozen snapshot, Smb2Dispatcher, NtlmServerMechanism, NtlmNegotiateMessage and SmbSession had changed. Failures were encrypted final SESSION_SETUP (two cases) and failure to disconnect on an invalid encrypted tag (one). This is separate evidence from the original frozen Microsoft REDs. That intermediate 26/29 result predates the completed auth repairs. The complete post-auth snapshot passed 29/29 under the same security settings. No native Windows, Wine, crossbuild or Native AOT execution is claimed by this task; the parent owns final native-host gates.

The latest complete JIT build succeeded with zero warnings/errors. `repaired-snapshot` includes all **2,641 registered cases present when captured**; no other owner's class/registration was excluded. The executed selections are explicitly **297 Microsoft cases: 297 PASS / 0 FAIL**, and **29 Go auth cases: 29 PASS / 0 FAIL**. These are selection results, not an all-harness or native-host gate. `repaired-list.txt`, `repaired-build.log`, `repaired-run.log` and `repaired-go-auth.log` retain the exact registrations and output. ### Retained exact compatibility RED, subsequently fixed

`upstream.microsoft.create.data-suffix-after-separators` sends a NON_DIRECTORY_FILE CREATE with six separators immediately before the unnamed `::$DATA` suffix. The independent expected status is **STATUS_OBJECT_NAME_INVALID (0xc0000033)**; the actual wire status is **STATUS_ACCESS_DENIED (0xc0000022)**. Source: [FSAModel CreateFileTestCaseS34](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsProtocolTestSuites/blob/29ddb4238a5443b7499e82934c90cc898861c5e7/TestSuites/FileServer/src/FSAModel/TestSuite/CreateFileTestCase.cs#L747), with the concrete filename construction in [FSAAdapter CreateFile](https://github.com/microsoft/WindowsProtocolTestSuites/blob/29ddb4238a5443b7499e82934c90cc898861c5e7/TestSuites/FileServer/src/FSA/Adapter/FSAAdapter.cs#L717).

Diagnosis on the captured source: `Smb2Dispatcher` checks `request.Name.EndsWith('\\')` before splitting streams. The DATA suffix makes that false, while the later parsed base name still ends with separators. The malformed pathname then reaches the host file open and maps to ACCESS_DENIED. A small compatibility repair is to apply the existing NON_DIRECTORY_FILE trailing-separator validation to the parsed base name before backend admission/mutation. This is a pinned FSA/Windows status-compatibility finding; implementation-specific SMB name-validation error choice is not mislabeled a universal SMB2 MUST. The next shared production snapshot adds this parsed-base-name check, and the unchanged case passes in `repaired-run.log`. The original RED and its source archive remain available; there is no unresolved Microsoft RED on the repaired snapshot. No production file was edited by this owner.

Kerberos KDC/SPN/keytab/domain tickets, Windows domain ACL/claims SUT control, physical NIC failover, SOFS/cluster nodes, NTFS/ReFS-only controls, arbitrary exported directional/finite-listener host pipes and unavailable optional feature grants remain concrete dispositions. They do not exclude ordinary supported commands. Source-only configuration/event bookkeeping is marked client-only in the input inventory. The independent [inventory audit](upstream-inventory-audit.md) qualifies the earlier per-row completeness assessment, corrects false exact mappings and records additional public cases. Source inventory classification alone does not prove all independent protocol facets are covered.

The serial owner's [repair report](upstream-repairs.md) independently records 297/297 Microsoft, 83/83 Go and 940/940 prior regressions. Only the Microsoft 297 and Go-auth 29 are this allocation's own latest executed selections. R07's overlong-name change is a Windows/FSA status-compatibility choice; the original FSA status is not imposed here as a portable SMB2 MUST. Cache/durable safety work and settled all-harness/native-host gates remain with their assigned owners.

<a id="d123"></a>**D123 — normative mismatch.** FSA requires INVALID_PARAMETER for DELETE_ON_CLOSE without DELETE desired access. MS-SMB2 requires the client to include DELETE but does not specify this exact server status for the invalid request; share maximal DELETE denial is separately a SHOULD. No ordinary successful deletion is misreported as this negative case.

<a id="d124"></a>**D124 — normative mismatch.** FSA prevalidation prioritizes zero DesiredAccess over its malformed trailing-separator pathname and requires ACCESS_DENIED.
